messages.author: 5e84f14a869dff98
messages.subject: Printing ggplot2 to WMF
parts:
Given current workflow and customer needs it would be really great if I could print out ggplot2 images as WMF. My example code is shown below. Please note, that I am able to successfully print to WMF outside of a loop, but for some reason inside a for loop the images are all blank (easy to reproduce this by commenting out the for loop stuff). Any thoughts or suggestions as it would be really helpful if I figured out what I am doing wrong?

Thanks again.

# Loop code that does not work.
VADeaths_flat_df = stack(as.data.frame(VADeaths))
names(VADeaths_flat_df) = c('Data','Person')
for(ii in 1:5)
{
VADeaths_title<-paste("C:/Images/VADeaths", ii,"_%02d.wmf", sep = "")
# Produce a Windows Meta File Format Plot
win.metafile(file=as.character(VADeaths_title), pointsize = 10)

counts <- ddply(VADeaths_flat_df, .(cut(Data, breaks=fullseq(range(Data), 20)), Person), nrow)
names(counts) <- c("bin", "person", "n")
qplot(person, n, data = counts, fill = person, geom="bar", stat="identity", width = 0.9) +
facet_grid(. ~ bin) + opts(axis.text.x = NULL) + opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(colour = "red")) +
opts(strip.text.x = theme_text(colour = "green", size=14))

dev.off()
}

messages.author: 4ddc99c6029ba75d
messages.subject: Re: Printing ggplot2 to WMF
parts: Not sure if this is doing what you want but I am able to print your graph as win.metafile. I think you have to use the 'print' statement before saving your graphics.

# Loop code that does not work.
VADeaths_flat_df = stack(as.data.frame(VADeaths))
names(VADeaths_flat_df) = c('Data','Person')

for(i in 1:5)
{
VADeaths_title<-paste("C:/Images/VADeaths", i,"_%02d.wmf", sep = "")
# Produce a Windows Meta File Format Plot
#win.metafile(file=as.character(VADeaths_title), pointsize = 10)

counts <- ddply(VADeaths_flat_df, .(cut(Data, breaks=fullseq(range(Data), 20)), Person), nrow)
names(counts) <- c("bin", "person", "n")
myplot <- qplot(person, n, data = counts, fill = person, geom="bar", stat="identity", width = 0.9) +

facet_grid(. ~ bin) + opts(axis.text.x = NULL) + opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(colour = "red")) +
opts(strip.text.x = theme_text(colour = "green", size=14))

win.metafile(filename="VADeaths.wmf",width=8.3,height=6.9,pointsize=9)
print(myplot)
dev.off()
}

messages.author: 5e84f14a869dff98
messages.subject: Need to add an empty bin group to bar plot
parts:
In order to keep the scales on plots for multiple data sets it appears that I need to add an empty bin in the bar plot.

I tried to do this in the example below by expanding the range, i.e. range(c(Data, max_range)) where max_range is the desired max x-scale, however apparently this had no effect. I hoped it would have added an "empty" bin from 80-100.

Thanks for your help.

VADeaths_flat_df = stack(as.data.frame(VADeaths))
names(VADeaths_flat_df) = c('Data','Person')

max_range<-100
counts <- ddply(VADeaths_flat_df, .(cut(Data, breaks=fullseq(range(c(Data, max_range)), 20)), Person), nrow)
names(counts) <- c("bin", "person", "n")

print(qplot(person, n, data = counts, fill = person, geom="bar", stat="identity", width = 0.9) + facet_grid(. ~ bin) + opts(axis.text.x = NULL) + opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(colour = "red")) + opts(strip.text.x = theme_text(colour = "green", size=14)))
